text:
Rae T: Quick post-GA triage: we have ~18 items flagged against streaming/resume. Need a fast decision framework so eng isn't juggling everything. Proposal: two lanes only for next 72h: HOTFIX (customer-blocking or >3% regression) and NEXT-SPRINT (everything else). Anything to add?

Priya M: Agree on 2 lanes. Suggest we add a "Revenue-impact" flag (enterprise customers with active SLAs) to always escalate to HOTFIX irrespective of % impact.

Owen L: +1. Also propose a tiny scoring formula to help ops: score = severity*2 + pct_sessions_affected + revenue_flag*10. If score >= 12 -> HOTFIX. Keeps it deterministic.

Diego H: Nice. Example: malformed event on reconnect (sev2, 2% sessions, no revenue flag) -> score = 2*2 + 2 = 6 -> NEXT-SPRINT.

Priya M: For customer asks (retry button UX), some customers asked for workaround now. Those map to enhancements unless a customer is blocked from production.

Rae T: OK. We'll run the scoring on the top 15 items and route them. Can we have SRE run quick sampling to validate pct_sessions numbers? nora-cs-bot: can you pull the 7-day reconnection error rates for the streaming consumer group?

nora-cs-bot: Query queued: telemetry.production.streams.errors.reconnect (7d). Returning sample window: 2026-03-14 to 2026-03-20. Top counts: reconnect-truncation=124 (0.9% sessions), kv-cache-miss=58 (0.4%), backpressure-deadlock=9 (0.06%).

Owen L: Great. Using that, only reconnect-truncation is borderline but below 3%. Recommend NEXT-SPRINT unless enterprise customer reported it.

Priya M: Which enterprise customers reported? Diego, can support tag the incidents?

Diego H: I pulled the CS tickets. Two customers A and B reported truncated streams; both are on dedicated plans. That triggers revenue_flag for those items.

Rae T: Then we have two HOTFIXes: RI-3010 (truncated reconnect for dedicated tenants) and RI-3022 (backpressure deadlock leading to client stalls; sev1 on 1 tenant). Others go to NEXT-SPRINT grooming.

Owen L: For hotfix delivery vehicle: small bundle w/ rollback to previous stream-lib. Canary in us-east for 1h then broader roll. We'll keep bundle scope minimal: one commit per fix, no behavioral changes to protocol.

Priya M: Acceptance criteria for hotfixes please (short checklist):
```
- Reproduce locally (unit/integration)
- Regression test on small replay dataset
- 95th pct latency within 10% of baseline
- Smoke test resume/reconnect across 3 tenants
- Customer confirm in ticket (if dedicated)
```

Rae T: Add one more: observability: create a dashboard tile showing reconnect success rate and session counts for the affected tenants.

Owen L: I'll own canary run + perf checks. deploy-bot: schedule canary window tonight at 02:00 UTC for us-east (1h).

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: hotfix-bundle-3010-3022 -> us-east at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z. Notifying eng-oncall.

Diego H: Communications: I'll draft a short customer note for A and B that we plan a canary fix and expect to be live in 4-6h after success. Priya, please review tone.

Priya M: Will review. Also splitting enhancement work for NEXT-SPRINT: retry-ux, docs for client reconnection best practices, and telemetry capture for reconnection patterns. Assigning to product board.

Rae T: Final action list: (1) Owen run canary + perf (owner: Owen), (2) Diego send customer advisory (owner: Diego), (3) Priya triage remaining 13 items with scoring and tag priorities (owner: Priya), (4) Product card for NEXT-SPRINT (owner: Rae). We'll sync if canary fails.

Owen L: Starting preflight now: collecting replay traces, smoke harness, perf baseline. Ping me for logs.

Rae T: Thanks team. If we get a clean canary, push these two as hotfixes and open follow-on enhancements for Sprint planning. Back to async unless escalation. :white_check_mark:
